Two Colors in Two Rows II

ParityInvariantsCounting
Game: Match colours between two rows of any length, even when they hold different numbers of reds.
How to play: Set the row length and the number of reds on top, then click two cells in a row to swap them.

Look for the math

The red and blue counts do not even need to match in the two rows — yet the number of links still does.

The weaker condition

All that is needed is that the reds on top equal the blues below (call that M₁), and the blues on top equal the reds below (M₂). The rows may be odd lengths and the two rows may have different numbers of red cells. The logic test checks every configuration satisfying this for rows up to length 6, and 500 random larger ones.

Two unmatched counts

If x columns join red to red and u join blue to blue, the unmatched reds on top number M₁ − x and sit above the unmatched blues below, which number M₁ − u. Hence M₁ − x = M₁ − u and x = u. Starting from M₂ gives the same result. The page likens this to pouring water and wine between two glasses: the amount of wine in the water glass equals the amount of water in the wine glass, because each glass ends with the same volume it began with.

Set the reds on top to a number that makes the two rows unequal. Does the link count still match?
